triage_candidates.statement: scripts/checklist_engine.py builds the Task shape by hand in TWO places -- _build_amend_task (~2105) and append() (~2317). They agree today (I diffed them by eye), but the new superset assertion reads only _build_amend_task, so a field added to append() alone stays invisible to the completeness property. One shared Task constructor would remove the class of drift.

The residual limit the class docstring states is live, not theoretical: 'anchors' is carried by shipped template JSON but emitted by neither _build_amend_task nor append() (verified by reading both). It sits in the fixture only because a human put it there. A check that walks the shipped templates' task objects for keys neither builder emits would close that hole mechanically.

Nothing checks docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md's Task table against what the engine actually builds. The new assertion binds the FIXTURE to the builder, not the DOC to the builder; the doc is currently stale on the directives row (declares [string] | null while all 8 populated corpus blocks are {name: {contract}}). A doc-vs-builder check would have caught that row itself. g3-schema fixes the row; this is about the missing guard.
